evals.prompt: Pak de critical op voor greenberrynl/refugeework/website uit de dependency scanner. (Context the agent can discover: the newest report.json lists next@16.3.0 on main with three critical advisories, fixedIn 16.3.3 and 16.3.6; development already runs next 16.3.8 and branches.diffs marks it fixedOn development. The project has merge_method ff and squash_option always, acceptance equals main, and docs/release-process.md has a hotfix runbook with a patch version, a CHANGELOG section, a tag and a GitLab Release. CONVENTIONS.md names no Slack channel. npm has published next 16.4.0 since development moved to 16.3.8. The local database carries a newer schema than main.)
evals.expected_output: The run reads report.json through the GitLab artifacts API rather than the Pages site, scopes the hotfix to the next criticals on main, and picks 16.3.8 because development already runs it within the same major. It installs the exact version (next@16.3.8), so the published 16.4.0 is not picked up. It validates locally before asking, building against a scratch database migrated with main's migrations instead of the developer's database. It plans the hotfix branch off origin/main, a patch version, changelog section, tag and release per the runbook, and announces the MR in #merge_requests without asking for a channel. Because squash_option is always, it plans the back-merge as pushes: a fast-forward of acceptance and a two-parent merge commit for development, and it explains that a squashed back-merge MR would break the ancestry. It shows one plan and waits for a single go before anything leaves the machine. The highs on development are listed as out of scope for npm-maintenance.
assertions: The report is read from the dependency-scanner job artifacts through glab api, not by fetching the Pages URL
Only the critical findings on the production branch are in the hotfix scope; highs are named as out of scope
The target version is 16.3.8, justified by development already running it in the same major
The back-merge plan uses pushes (fast-forward for acceptance, merge commit for development), not squashed MRs, with the ancestry reason stated
The install uses the exact version next@16.3.8, not a caret range, and the lockfile ends on 16.3.8
The production build runs against a scratch database with main's schema, not the developer's local database
The Slack plan names #merge_requests and the run does not ask for a channel
No MR, push or Slack post happens before the single go on the plan

evals.prompt: Critical in the scanner for greenberrynl/client/shop: handlebars 3.0.8 on main, fixedIn 4.7.9. Hotfix it.
evals.expected_output: The run sees that the only fix crosses a major (3 → 4), so it is not a hotfix candidate. It stops before creating a branch, reports the advisory and the major jump, and routes the upgrade to the researched major-version path of npm-maintenance. It posts nothing to Slack and opens no MR.
assertions: The run identifies that the fix requires a major version upgrade
The run stops before creating a branch, worktree or MR
The run routes the change to npm-maintenance's major-version workflow

evals.prompt: Resume the dependency hotfix for greenberrynl/client/site. (Context: hotfix MR !88 merged and deployed; the push back-merge into acceptance succeeded; git merge-tree for development reports conflicts in package-lock.json and in src/lib/http.ts.)
evals.expected_output: Step 0 finds the merged hotfix MR and resumes at the back-merge. Acceptance already contains production and is skipped. For development the run sees a conflict outside the files it may resolve (src/lib/http.ts), so it leaves development untouched, reports both conflicted paths, posts that the back-merge into development needs a human in the Slack thread, and does not resolve the source conflict itself.
assertions: The run resumes from the merged MR instead of starting a new hotfix
Acceptance is detected as already containing production and skipped
The run does not resolve the conflict in src/lib/http.ts
The development branch is left untouched and the conflicted paths are reported
The Slack thread gets a reply saying the development back-merge needs a human
